| Item | Fact |

| MPC members | 6 - Governor (chair), a Deputy Governor, one RBI officer + 3 Government nominees; Governor has the casting vote (not chaired by a Deputy Governor) |
| External members | Serve 4 years; quorum 4; MPC meets at least 4 times a year |
| Law | RBI Act, 1934, amended by the Finance Act, 2016 (May 2016) - Flexible Inflation Targeting; Monetary Policy Framework Agreement February 2015; MPC constituted September 2016 |
| Section 45ZB | Creates the MPC |
| Section 45ZA | Inflation target - CPI 4% ± 2% (target is 4%, not 2%), set by the Centre in consultation with RBI, every 5 years |
| Section 45ZN | Failure = 3 consecutive quarters outside the band (8 Sep 2026) |
| Basis point | 1 bps = 0.01% |
- **RBI**: established **1 April 1935** (under the RBI Act, 1934); **nationalised 1949**; HQ **Mumbai**; Governor **Sanjay Malhotra**.
- **Repo rate held at 5.25%** in April 2026 – pause after ~125 bps cuts from early 2025; FY 2026–27 inflation estimate **4.6%**. Governor **Sanjay Malhotra**.
- **RBI projections (October 2026 policy, repo raised to 5.50%):** FY27 real GDP **7.1%**; FY27 CPI **5.2%**.

- **Small savings rates for Oct-Dec 2026 kept unchanged** (Finance Ministry, 30 Sep 2026): **Sukanya Samriddhi 8.2%** (highest, with **SCSS 8.2%**), **NSC 7.7%**, **KVP 7.5%** (matures in 115 months), **POMIS 7.4%**, **PPF 7.1%**, **3-year Time Deposit 7.1%**, **5-year RD 6.7%**, **post office savings 4%** - the same rates every quarter since 2024 (Oct-Dec 2025, Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep 2026).

- **EPF interest rate 2025-26: 8.25%** - recommended by the EPFO **Central Board of Trustees** (2 Mar 2026; chaired by Labour Minister **Mansukh Mandaviya**), approved by the **Finance Ministry**, ratified June 2026, notified by EPFO 1 Jul 2026; **third straight year** at 8.25% (2023-24 and 2024-25 also 8.25%; 2024-25 rate fixed 28 Feb 2025, Finance Ministry concurrence May 2025).
# Small savings

- Final estimates for **2022-23 and 2023-24**; first revised estimates for **2024-25**; revised indicators for 2025-26.
- **FY 2025-26 real growth, revised:** **7.4%** (NSO First Advance Estimate, Jan 2026; also the Economic Survey figure) → **7.6%** (new series, 27 Feb 2026) → **7.7%** (Provisional Estimates, June 2026; GVA 7.9%) → **7.8%** (NAS 2026). Older figures for 2023-24 / 2024-25 were 7.2% / 7.1% (nominal 11% / 9.7%).

- **New base year 2022-23** (from **2011-12**), introduced **27 February 2026** - the **ninth base revision** (earlier bases 1948-49, 1960-61, 1970-71, 1980-81, 1993-94, 1999-2000, 2004-05, 2011-12); adds **GST and vehicle registration data**; nominal GDP revised down 2.7-3.8%.

| Concept | Economic Survey |
|---|---|
| Chakravyuha challenge (easy entry but hard exit of firms) | 2015-16 (CEA Arvind Subramanian) |
| Universal Basic Income | 2016-17 |
| Thalinomics | 2019-20 |
| Bare Necessities Index (water, sanitation, housing, micro-environment and other facilities) | 2020-21 |
- **North East**: Buddhist circuits in Arunachal, Sikkim, Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura (Purvodaya items – see the Purvodaya overview).

- **Urban Challenge Fund**: announced in **Union Budget 2025-26**; **₹1 lakh crore**; cities as growth hubs – funds up to **25% of the cost of bankable projects** (**Centre 25%, States 25%, market 50%**); ₹10,000 crore for 2025-26; ₹4 lakh crore investment in 5 years; FY 2025–26 to 2030–31; MoHUA.

- **Makhana** (*Euryale ferox*) – edible **seed (fox nut)**; **Bihar** ~3/4 of India; **Makhana Board in Bihar** announced in **Union Budget 2025-26** (production, processing, marketing) – **National Makhana Board** launched in Bihar 15 September 2025; **DGFT** gave separate HSN codes; NRC Makhana – varieties, makhana-cum-fish farming, popping machines.
- **NRLM 2010** (restructured **SGSY**).
- MSMEs: **62% of employment**; ~95% of registered units micro or small ("missing middle").
- **Udyam Registration Portal: 1 July 2020** (free, paperless); Udyam Assist Platform 11 January 2023.
- **Economic Survey 2025-26**: MSMEs = **31.1% of GDP**, **35.4%** of manufacturing output, **48.58%** of exports (earlier estimates: 30.1% of GDP, 45.73% of exports).

- Udyam + Udyam Assist (6 Oct 2026): ~**9.78 crore** registrations (7.30 crore+ in Dec 2025); **43.28 crore** jobs; women-owned **37.6%**; trading 4.08 crore, services 3.77 crore, manufacturing 1.93 crore.
- CGTMSE cover up to ₹10 crore. **Cyber Jagrit Bharat** with **CERT-In**; **ODR Portal** – delayed payments; **Yashasvini** – women-owned MSMEs.
- **Atal Innovation Mission**: **2016, NITI Aayog**; ₹2,750 crore (till 2028); 10,000+ ATLs.
- Kisan e-Mitra (voice AI chatbot, 11 languages); **National Pest Surveillance System – 65 crops, 400+ pests**; **SATHI** – Seed Authenticity Traceability & Holistic Inventory (National Seed Grid).

- **India's first collective domestic platform** for insuring large maritime risks – Indian vessels on **high-risk/war-affected routes (West Asia)**; cuts reliance on the London-based **International Group of P&I Clubs**.
- Administrator: **General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)** (est. 1972, Mumbai); under the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways**; regulator **IRDAI** (Insurance Act, 1938).

- **Export Promotion Mission**: **Department of Commerce**; **₹25,060 crore** (2025–26 to 2030–31); MSME focus; **Niryat Protsahan** (finance/credit – pilots: interest subvention on pre- and post-shipment credit, collateral support) and **Niryat Disha** (market access).

- **PM E-DRIVE** (Ministry of Heavy Industries; Cabinet September 2024, from **1 Oct 2024**; outlay **₹10,900 crore** – not ₹10,000 crore, which was FAME-II; replaced FAME-II and EMPS 2024): **₹2,000 crore** for charging – guidelines **28 September 2025** give **up to 100% subsidy** for EV charging, battery swapping and battery charging stations; e-2W subsidy to **31 July 2026** (March 2026 extension; later extended to **31 March 2028**, Aug 2026); e-rickshaw/e-cart to **31 March 2028**.

- **BHAVYA Rasayan** (Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana - Rasayan, July 2026): **three mega chemical parks**, each **≥ 8 sq km (2,000 acres)**; Centre up to **₹1,000 crore per park** (State min **₹500 crore**); outlay **₹3,030 crore**; common effluent treatment plants (CETPs); for pharma, electronics, textiles.
- Approved by the Union Cabinet (**31 July 2026**; reported August 2026); **Central Sector Scheme** of the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**; guidelines issued **25 Oct 2026**.

- Outlay **₹84,084 crore** up to **2030-31** - for **offshore oil and gas** in deepwater and ultra-deepwater (**56 exploratory and 4 stratigraphic wells**), not seabed minerals (differs from the Sagar Manthan vessel).

- **Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (RCS-UDAN):** launched **21 October 2016**; first flight **Shimla-Delhi, 27 April 2017**; fare cap about **₹2,500** for a one-hour / ~500 km flight; **687 routes**, 95 airports (Oct 2026) - up from 625 routes, 90 airports, 15 heliports and 2 water aerodromes (Dec 2025; 1.49 crore+ passengers; 102 new routes in 2024); operational airports **74 (2014) → 165 (July 2026)**.

- **Modified UDAN:** Cabinet 25 March 2026, **₹28,840 crore** for 10 years (**2026-27 to 2035-36**) - **100 new airports** (₹12,159 crore), heliports and water aerodromes, **200 helipads**; launched at **Jodhpur** Airport, 4 July 2026.

- **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan**: launched **13 October 2021** by PM Modi; **5 years** on 13 Oct 2026; **GIS platform** connecting **58 Central Ministries** (16 infrastructure ministries at launch) and all **36 States/UTs**; nodal **DPIIT**; **7 sectors** (railways, roads, ports, waterways, airports, mass transport, logistics infra - **not telecom**). **National Logistics Policy: 17 Sep 2022**; ITLA appraises projects of **₹500 crore+**.

- **PM Gati Shakti**: subsumes National Infrastructure Pipeline (₹110 lakh crore, 2019); 11 industrial corridors, 2 defence corridors (Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh); 17,000 km gas pipeline addition; logistics cost ~**13% of GDP**.

- SCBs – Second Schedule of RBI Act, 1934.
- Components: **Foreign Currency Assets (FCA, the largest), gold, SDRs, Reserve Tranche Position (RTP)** with the IMF; **held by RBI, owned by the Government of India**.

- **China overtook the USA as India's biggest trading partner in 2025–26**: trade **$151.1 bn**; **deficit $112.16 bn**; imports $131.63 bn, exports $19.47 bn. (In 2024-25 the **USA** was the largest for the **fourth year in a row** – $131.84 bn, exports $86.51 bn; China second at $127.7 bn with a record deficit of $99.2 bn.)

- **Rice**: India **overtook China as largest producer** – **150.18 MT vs 145.28 MT (2024–25)**, announced by Shivraj Singh Chouhan; largest exporter since 2011–12 (21.69 MT in 2024–25); paddy ~2,000 L/kg, milled rice ~3,000 L/kg.

- **Rice trade**: ~40% of global rice trade; exports 198.65 lakh t (**$12.95 bn**, FY 2024-25 – **India's largest agricultural export**) to 172 countries; **India's share in US rice imports 26.1% (2024)**.

- **APEDA**: 40th anniversary – **APEDA Act, 1985**, operative **13 February 1986**; Ministry of Commerce; HQ New Delhi; runs NPOP; Agriculture Export Policy 2018; ODOP. **First export of GI Salem Sago** – 0.5 MT to **Canada** (SAGOSERVE).
- Seafood FY26: ₹72,325 crore, 19.32 lakh t; **top port Visakhapatnam** (then JNPT, Kochi, Kolkata, Chennai); **EU = 3rd-largest seafood market** (after US, China) – US$1.593 bn.
- Seafood exports 2025–26 mainly to **USA and China**. India–France target **USD 32 billion** in five years.

- **Soil Health Card (2015):** 25 crore+ cards; every **2 years**, 12 parameters; linked to the **National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture**. **RKVY 2007**. **NAFCC: 100% central grant** (not 55%).

- **Milk 2024–25: 247.87 MMT** (2023–24: 239.3 MMT) – **world's largest producer**, ~25% of world output; per capita **485 g/day** (459 g in 2023–24); dairy ~3.5% of GDP; meat **4th**; livestock CAGR **12.77%**.

- **Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme** (since 2003, MoPNG): Roadmap 2020–25 moved E20 from **2030 → 2025** (achieved); **E20 petrol mandatory nationwide from 1 April 2026** (RON 95); E20 = 20% ethanol (E100 = pure ethanol); **no proposal at present to go beyond E20**.
- **Green Hydrogen Certification Portal (GHCI):** certification, standardisation, compliance of green hydrogen; operational **1 July 2026**.
- Related: **Clydebank Declaration** (green corridors) - **COP26 Glasgow 2021**; **IMO** est. **1948**, **London**; EU - Maastricht Treaty, 1 Nov 1993, 27 members; Sagarmala 2015.

- **Central Sector Scheme** (Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas): **₹23,731 crore** over 10 years, **2026-27 to 2035-36**; Cabinet 6 Aug 2026, launched 1 Oct 2026.
- **CBG blending obligation** (CNG/PNG, City Gas Distribution): **3% (2026-27), 4% (2027-28), 5% from 2028-29**; administered price ₹2,110 per MMBTU; capital aid up to ₹2 crore per tonne-per-day; credit guarantee for MSME CBG projects; pipeline support.
- **Plants (Aug 2026):** 1,929 registered, 217 commissioned, 357 under construction.
# Compressed biogas – existing schemes

- **PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana** (**13 February 2024**, **MNRE** – Minister Pralhad Joshi; National Solar Mission 2010): rooftop solar for **1 crore households by FY 2026-27** (target 30 GW); **free power up to 300 units a month**; subsidy ₹30,000–60,000 (1–2 kW), ₹60,000–78,000 (2–3 kW), **₹78,000 max (above 3 kW)**; pace to reach **1 lakh rooftops every 5 days** (Nov 2026).
- Progress: 26.19 lakh+ systems (19 March 2026) → **40 lakh+ households (May 2026)**; grid-connected rooftop capacity 26.75 GW (30 April 2026; ~82% of Q1 2026 additions residential); leading States **Gujarat, Maharashtra, UP, Kerala**; Budget 2026-27 **₹22,000 crore (+29.4%)**; **World Bank $890 million + ADB $850 million**; 3 lakh+ skilled manpower.
- Rooftop solar 24 GW (2026) → 41+ GW by 2030.
- Pumped hydro 50 GW within six years.

- **Deposit-free LPG connection to adult women of poor households**; launched at **Ballia (UP)**; 8 crore connections by September 2019; **Ujjwala 2.0 (August 2021)** +1 crore; **10.57 crore** connections (10.35 crore on 1 Dec 2025; 25 lakh more approved for FY 2025-26); a single **Deprivation Declaration** replaced the multi-point self-declaration; 2025-26 targeted subsidy ₹12,000 crore.

- **Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** (MoSJE – Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar; **15 August 2020** in 272 districts, nationwide 2023; flagship of **NAPDDR**, run through **NISD**): reached **35.84 crore people** (14.33 crore youth, 11.32 crore women) as on 10 Nov 2026 (29.32 crore in mid-2026).

- About **1.2 crore** girls a year (one-liners also say "girls under 14"); the 28 Feb 2026 launch is often reported as March 2026.
- Indigenous **Cervavac** is **not yet WHO-approved** for the programme.

- **NVHCP (2018)** covers Hepatitis **A, B, C, D, E**; goal: **eliminate Hepatitis B and C by 2030 (SDG 3.3)**; free diagnostics and drugs; NVHCP-MIS portal; 21.06 crore screened; 6.12 lakh B and C patients treated; 1,153 treatment sites.
- New TB case rate 2015-2024: **India -21%**.
- **West Bengal** became the **36th State/UT** to implement **AB PM-JAY** (**8 June 2026**); Ayushman Bharat (2018) = PM-JAY + Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.
- **PMJAY (2018, Ayushman Bharat)**: **private hospitals** get **two-thirds** of PMJAY spending.

- **ULLAS** = **Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society** (New India Literacy Programme / Nav Bharat Saksharta): launched **2022** by the Union Education Ministry; CSS, 2022-23 to 2026-27; goal 100% literacy by **2030**; adults **15 years and above**; literacy up to **Class 3** level, then test (**FLNAT**) and certification; slogan "**Jan Jan Sakshar**".
- **"Fully literate"** = at least **95%** literacy among people aged 15+ (benchmark of August 2024).

| Unit | Status |
|---|---|
| **Ladakh** | First UT fully functionally literate (**24 June 2024**) |
| **Mizoram** | First **State** fully literate (20 May 2025) |
| Goa, Tripura | 2nd and 3rd States |
| Himachal Pradesh | 4th State – 99.30%, declared on International Literacy Day (8 Sept 2025) at the ULLAS Mela, Shimla |
| Sikkim | 5th State (27 May 2026) |
| Uttarakhand | 6th State, 8 July 2026 (98.7%) |
| J&K | Fully literate, September 2026 |
| **Lakshadweep** | First UT with **100%** literacy, **11 October 2026** (capital **Kavaratti**) |

- **PM-SHRI** = Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India: launched **7 September 2022**, **CSS**, 2022-23 to 2026-27; cost **₹27,360 crore** (central share **₹18,128 crore**); **14,500+ schools** as NEP exemplars; 18 lakh+ students.
- **Selection:** **3-stage Challenge Mode using UDISE+**; **max 2 schools per block/ULB**; monitored by **School Quality Assessment Framework**.
- **Launched 17 September 2023**; Central Sector; nodal **Ministry of MSME**; **₹13,000 crore**, 2023-24 to 2027-28; **18 traditional trades**; 30 lakh registrations in two years (Dec 2025).

| Component | Provision |
|---|---|
| Training stipend | **₹500 a day** |
| Toolkit | **Up to ₹15,000** (as an e-voucher) |
| Loan | Collateral-free **up to ₹3 lakh** (₹1 lakh + ₹2 lakh tranches) at **5%** |

- **Outlay ₹60,000 crore** over five years = ₹30,000 crore Centre + ₹20,000 crore States + **₹10,000 crore industry**; **World Bank and ADB co-finance 50% of the central share** (not all of it); modernises **1,000 ITIs** in hub-and-spoke clusters with **five National CoEs**; nationwide approval **7 July 2026**; ₹1,237.58 crore cluster plans in Odisha, Gujarat, Telangana; MSDE Minister **Jayant Chaudhary**.

- At least **25%** of total balance must remain (max ~75% withdrawable); most withdrawals after 12 months of membership; premature final settlement wait raised **2 → 12 months** (under Para 69(2) of the 1952 Scheme, full withdrawal was allowed after two months of unemployment).

- **Dates:** launched **24 February 2019**, effective from **1 December 2018**; **Central Sector Scheme** (100% Centre), Ministry of Agriculture; continued for **2026-27 to 2030-31** with outlay **₹3.15 lakh crore** (Cabinet, Aug 2026); all landholding farmer families; **income-tax payers** and most government employees **excluded**.
- **Har Ghar Jal** – announced **15 August 2019**; Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, **Ministry of Jal Shakti**; original target every rural household by **2024**.
- Deadline extended from **2024 to December 2028** as **JJM 2.0** (Cabinet, March 2026) to cover all **19.36 crore** rural households.
# Jal Jeevan Mission – Phase I and Sujalam Bharat

- **India's first cooperative-based ride-hailing (mobility) platform**; set up **6 June 2025** under the **Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002**; run by **Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Ltd**; launched by **Amit Shah** on **5 February 2026**.
- **Co-Keralam:** Kerala's proposed first cooperative airline, from **Kochi**.
# Cabinet decisions - 11 Nov 2026 (Stand-Up India extension: see the schemes notes)
- **Musi Riverfront Phase-I**: ADB in-principle loan ₹4,100 crore (USD 500 million), 2 January 2026; Phase-I 21 km (project 55 km within HMDA limits); CM **A. Revanth Reddy**.

- **PAIMANA** (Project Assessment Infrastructure Monitoring and Analytics for Nation-Building) – by **MoSPI**; mandatory for Central Sector projects of **₹150 crore+**; replaced OCMS-2006; April 2026 – 1,981 projects worth ~₹43 lakh crore; "One Data – One Entry"; ~60% updates automated.

- **Noida International Airport (Jewar)** Phase 1 inaugurated **28 March 2026** (see the Sep–Nov 2026 entry). **Nagpur Airport** international under PPP – GMR. **CWC** 70th foundation day 2 March 2026 (est. 1957). PRISM-SG portal for rail over-bridge girders.

- **Noida (Jewar) airport**: UP Cabinet (**9 Oct 2026**) proposed the name **"Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar"** (Gautam Buddha Nagar), marking Modi's 25 years as head of government; **final decision by the Union Cabinet + Gazette notification**; greenfield **PPP**, developed by **YIAPL**; phase 1 inaugurated **28 March 2026**; commercial flights from **15 June 2026**. **AAI** est. 1 April 1995.
- **Steel**: India **2nd-largest producer since 2018**; share 5.2% → 7.9%; consumption 163.7 MT (2025–26).
- Automobile – largest 2W/3W market; pharma 3rd by volume; defence production ₹1.54 lakh crore, exports ₹23,622 crore; **Defence Industrial Corridors – UP and Tamil Nadu**.

- **Make in India - 12 years**: launched **25 September 2014**; **DPIIT**; **27 sectors** (15 manufacturing + 12 services); logo - **lion of gear wheels**; electronics production ~**₹13.11 lakh crore** (2025-26, from ~₹1.9 lakh crore in 2014-15); mobile phones ₹18,000 crore to ₹6.27 lakh crore (2025-26); India **2nd-largest mobile-phone maker by volume**.
- ₹1.09 lakh crore to the **Contingency Fund** – meant for **financial and monetary risks** (balance sheet ₹91.97 lakh crore – see the RBI dividend entry).

- **Atmanirbhar Panchayat / SAMARTH Panchayat Portal:** raise **Own Source Revenue** of PRIs (taxes, fees, rents, service charges); digitise property tax, licences; being expanded to **Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra**.

- **Namo Drone Didi:** **Central Sector Scheme** (₹1,261 crore) – women SHGs get agri-drones under **DAY-NRLM**; **Karnataka** leads in training; 15,000 drones in 2024-26; **80% subsidy up to ₹8 lakh**, rest via **AIF with 3% interest subvention**; 15-day drone pilot training for one woman per SHG.
- **Rural broadband:** only ~**8%** of rural households have broadband (a constraint for Namo Drone Didi and digital agriculture).
- **Agri Param:** agri language model (Bharat-VISTAAR – see the Dec 2025–Feb 2026 entry).
# Next-Generation GST reforms (56th meeting, effective September 2025) – other changes

| Item | Fact |
|---|---|
| In force | 1 July 2017 |
| Amendment | 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 |
| GST Council | Article 279A (not 280); constituted 2016 by the President; chaired by the Union Finance Minister (Nirmala Sitharaman) |
| Voting | Three-fourths of weighted votes; Centre one-third, States two-thirds |
| Quorum | Half of members |
| Taxes | CGST, SGST/UTGST, IGST |
| Nature | Destination-based |
| Offences, prosecution, arrest | CGST Act, 2017 |
- GST February 2026: **₹1.83 lakh crore**; FY up to 28 Feb **₹20.27 lakh crore** (+8.3%).
- Taxpayers 1.6 crore+ (Jan 2026); GST 2.0 – two-rate structure.
